- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.30), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast bias by 5–10% relative to recent mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior 7-day high), model often overshoots; cap forecast peak at 1.5x prior high or 10% below recent 30d high.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending down, model underreacts; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% to align with sentiment momentum.
- Mean reversion is stronger in low-volatility periods (sentiment < -0.20); model should revert to 14-day moving average within 3–5 days of deviation.
- Forecast horizon >14 days shows persistent lag; add 1–2% lag correction for each additional day beyond 14.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer for downside tail risk.
